junction.name: South Van Ness Avenue & 13th Street, San Francisco

claims.text: South Van Ness Avenue & 13th Street had 27 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are South Van Ness Avenue & 13th Street's own: the city's record places 19 of the 46 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.8 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got continental crosswalks in 2019. Across the city: at 780 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+4%, 95% interval -25% to +33%) could be zero. The city's own record neither shows it worked nor rules it out, so repeating it here rests on other evidence.
The city's painted safety zones: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+2%, 95% interval -20% to +34%) could be zero); a second run of the same design on 780 sites agrees.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.8 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $277,000 a year.
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.1 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $36,000 a year.
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is responsible for 13th Street, Erie Street, Howard Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) (route designation only; confirm ownership) is responsible for South Van Ness Avenue (signed route in OpenStreetMap; owner not confirmed).

A request letter to the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) and the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) (route designation only; confirm ownership) is ready to draft from these facts.
